description.text:
The objective of this project was to determine patterns in the Global Terrorism Database using different data mining techniques.The analysis was carried in three different parts. 

1.The first part of analysis is to uncover patterns in attack type in different regions using association rule.

2. Second part of analysis is to predict the inclusion criterion of terrorist activity: political, economic, religious, social, three different SVM models were built for these three criteria, each with three different samples, and results were validated on test set.

3. Finally, the last part of analysis is to determine if the group name associated with terrorist activity the results were proven on a subset of data using Random Forest Classifier and tuning the model.

projects.title: Insurance Planner - Data Administration Concepts and Database Management Project
projects.subtitle: Nov 2015 - Nov 2015

description.text:
Insurance is something every individual needs, it helps to cover ones medical/damage expenses but choosing the right plan can be overwhelming. Most people in the United States have health insurance through their employer or union. Others seek out an individual or family health plan through a healthcare exchange, an agent, an insurance company, or a broker. The main purpose of the project is to centralize all the available insurance be it health, car or cosmetic in one place. 

The current system works such a way that the customer has to get in touch with an agent from each insurance company and gains knowledge about the policy or plan offered by that company. The database developed is an user interactive database where in the customer can make more informed decision based on the plan available without the help of a third person. With amalgamation of all the insurance plan provided by different company in single centralized database would make it easier for the customers to choose the best plan by comparing them online. The database is designed such a way that customer can query the database by his or her own needs and also gives the customer with all available schemes or plan offered by different insurance companies in one place.

projects.title: Enhanced S-Box design based on chaos theory
projects.subtitle: Dec 2011 - Dec 2011

description.text: Associated with Shanmugha Arts, Science, Technology and Research Academy

The project deals with the designing of a dynamic S-box based on the Chaos Theory. Chaotic maps are used to design S-box and offer computational efficiency in the design process. The S-box generates random numbers which can be used for encryption algorithms like AES and DES. These random numbers were run against few tests and the statistical results were shown as a graph.

projects.title: Hypothesis Testing: University town prices of USA - Python
projects.subtitle: Feb 2017 - Mar 2017

description.text:
1. Hypothesis: University towns have their mean housing prices less effected by recessions. 

2. Ran a t-test comparing the university town values to the non-university towns values, return whether the alternative hypothesis (that the two groups are the same) is true or not as well as the p-value of the confidence. 

3. Rejected the null hypothesis on University towns mean housing prices have same effects as non-University town mean housing prices during recessions with 99% confidence and p-value 0.002099

Dataset used:
1.From the Zillow research data site there is housing data for the United States which has median home sale prices at a fine grained level

2.From the Wikipedia page on college towns is a list of university towns in the United States

3.From Bureau of Economic Analysis, US Department of Commerce, the GDP over time of the United States in current dollars (used the chained value in 2009 dollars), note :considered GDP data from the first quarter of 2000 onward.
